MESSAGE:
I run deliveries for a small furniture restorer and I've got a few things to sort for tomorrow.

Can you suggest a name for our new delivery van (staff vote, nothing rude)?

Tomorrow the van can't leave the depot before 08:30 and must be back by 12:00. Three drops, each takes 15 minutes to unload. Drop A has a delivery window of 09:00 to 10:00. Drop B is a shop that needs its delivery done before it opens at 09:30. Drop C is an office that won't accept anything before 11:00. Driving times: depot to A 30 min, depot to B 20 min, depot to C 45 min, A to B 25 min, A to C 40 min, B to C 50 min. The driver also needs a 30-minute break somewhere before 12:00. What order should he go in, and what's the timeline?

Could you also rewrite our delivery text so it sounds friendlier than "Driver arriving. Be in."? List three things the driver should check on furniture before handing it over. Should we give customers a paper delivery note or an emailed one? And define "proof of delivery" in a line for our new part-timer. One more thing: we're thinking of texting customers the evening before with a rough arrival time. Could you draft that evening-before text too, keeping it under 160 characters so it goes as a single message?

REQUESTS:
1. Suggest a name for the delivery van
2. Work out the drop order and timeline meeting all time windows, the break and the 12:00 return  KEY: Only feasible order is B -> A -> C. Leave 08:30, arrive B 08:50, unload to 09:05 (done before 09:30); arrive A 09:30, unload to 09:45 (inside 09:00-10:00); arrive C 10:25, wait until 11:00 (take the 30-min break during this wait); unload 11:00-11:15; back at depot 12:00 exactly (zero slack). A-first fails (B reached 09:40, after opening). Must give order B, A, C with a timeline that respects all constraints.
3. Rewrite the delivery text to be friendlier
4. List three furniture checks before handover
5. Recommend paper vs emailed delivery note
6. Define 'proof of delivery' in a line
7. Draft an evening-before arrival text under 160 characters

ANSWER:
## Van names

- **Van Gogh** (a natural fit for a restorer)
- **Chester Drawers**
- **Sofa So Good**
- **Vincent Van Go**

## Route: B, then A, then C (the only order that works)

- **B must come first.** It has to be finished before 09:30.
- **A must come before C.** If the driver goes to A first, he reaches B at 09:40, which is too late. And C can't take anything before 11:00, so it has to be last.

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| 08:30 | Leave depot |
| 08:50 | Arrive at **B** and unload |
| 09:05 | Leave B |
| 09:30 | Arrive at **A** (window 09:00–10:00) and unload |
| 09:45 | Leave A |
| 10:25 | Arrive near **C**. **30-minute break**, 10:25–10:55 |
| 11:00 | Unload at **C** as soon as they accept deliveries |
| 11:15 | Leave C |
| **12:00** | **Back at depot** |

**There is no spare time on the return.** C can't be done before 11:00, unloading takes 15 minutes, and the drive back takes 45, so 12:00 is the earliest possible return whatever order you choose. If C keeps him waiting even five minutes, or the traffic is bad, he'll be late. Options:
- Ask C whether they'd accept a little earlier, say 10:45.
- Check whether returning at around 12:00 is acceptable.
- Brief the driver so he isn't caught out.

## Friendlier arrival text

> "Hi [Name], it's [Driver] from [Company]. I'm on my way with your furniture and should be with you in about [20] minutes. See you soon!"

## Three things to check before handing furniture over

1. **Condition.** Look for scratches, dents or marks to the finish picked up in transit, and compare against how it left the workshop.
2. **Everything is there.** Shelves, keys, handles, glass panels, feet, and any loose fittings.
3. **It works and sits properly.** Drawers and doors open smoothly, and it stands level without rocking once it's in place.

Ideally, have the customer look it over with the driver before signing.

## Paper or emailed delivery note?

**Emailed, with a signature captured on the driver's phone.** It's quicker, it can't get lost, and you can find it later if there's a dispute. Keep a few paper notes in the van for customers who'd prefer one or don't use email.

## Proof of delivery, for the new part-timer

> "Proof of delivery is the record, usually the customer's signature, with the date, time and a photo, showing the item was delivered in good condition to the right person."

## Evening-before text

> "Hi Sam, your Oakwood delivery is due tomorrow between 9 and 10am. We'll text when the driver is on the way. Any questions, call 01234 567890."

With those example details, it's **141 characters**, so you have a little room for longer names.

**One thing to watch:** use a plain straight apostrophe (') in "We'll". A curly apostrophe (’), emojis or certain special characters switch the message to a different format with a **70-character** limit, so this text would go as three messages instead of one.
